evidence: Swap test fails: an equipment-hire shop, a library-of-things in another town or a council bulky-waste booking could use this frame unchanged; only the words (tool names, deposits, 'Open' sessions, Mill Lane address) bind it to Fernhill.

Identity-carrying elements are portable: the brand is a stock wrench line icon plus 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body sans (header, all routes); every tool card on / uses the same wrench glyph on a pale green square as its image (10 identical tiles at 1280 and 375); colour is one forest-green accent on an off-white/grey ground; headings are the body sans in bold.

Category-guess fails: predicted default for a community booking/reservation service is a public-service style form page (white/grey ground, one green or blue accent, bold sans headings, bordered cards, native controls) and that is what renders.
Similar-prompt fails: a brief for 'a community seed library's reservation page' would land on the same green accent, icon tiles, card list and month grid.

Only the session calendar on /tool.html (days marked 'Open', dots at 375) and the copy ('returned when it comes back clean and working', 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower') come from this product's mechanism, and the calendar is a stock month grid with a label.

evidence: Clean and orderly, consistent green-on-off-white system, decent dark theme, but nothing on any main screen rewards a look.
The find page is a heading, a paragraph, a search field and ten identical placeholder-icon cards; basket, confirm and done are default form pages with a bordered summary box.
No imagery of tools, no drawn device; colour only marks buttons and availability badges. The member planning a weekend job sees a competent form, not the library they belong to.
